messages:
incident-bot: [PAGER] High 5xx rate detected on /v1/generate (us-east-1). Alert threshold crossed: 18% error rate over 3m. Pager dispatched to @ben (oncall). Incident ID: INC-20260315-1042

ben (oncall): Saw the page, moving to incident channel. I’m pulling logs and tracing now. Assigning myself as incident lead.

alice (SRE): Ben — ping when you have an initial hypothesis. I’ll stand by to throttle traffic & provision fallback.

ben (oncall): Quick glance at api-gateway logs: increased 429s from a downstream cache, but 5xx spike originates from model-proxy returning 503s. Rolling back last deploy? Deploy-bot shows no recent deploys to prod in past 2h.

carla (ops): Noted. I’m checking GPU pool health and infra autoscaler. No node restarts in last hour in us-east-1.

dan (prodeng): Could be a target model OOM pattern — logs show memory pressure on model-node-17. If it's KV-cache eviction thrash we can route traffic to warm pool.

ben (oncall): Mitigation plan: (1) enable routing fallback to v1-generate-lite (quantized) in us-east-1; (2) enable prefix KV-cache bypass for requests older than 1s to reduce cache churn; (3) update status page pending customer impact. Executing 1 now.

carla (ops): Executed routing change. Canary to 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 4m. Monitoring latency & 5xx.

ben (oncall): Progress: 10% -> 50% now. Errors dropping to ~6%. Will continue ramp.

alice (SRE): Good. Start drafting status page text with impact window and affected regions. Elaine looped for comms copy.

elaine (commops): Drafting status page and customer notice. Need severity level — suggestions? Is this degraded (partial outage) or major?

dan (prodeng): I'd call it "partial outage" for us-east-1 API generation with degraded success rate for some model variants. Affects hosted customers using default routing in us-east-1. No data loss.

elaine (commops): Draft status update (first pass):

```
Incident INC-20260315-1042: Partial outage in us-east-1 affecting text generation (2026-03-15T02:14 UTC)
Summary: We are investigating increased error rates for /v1/generate in the us-east-1 region. Some requests are failing with 5xx responses. A mitigation (routing to a quantized fallback model) is being deployed. Customers in us-east-1 may experience increased latency or errors.
Impact: Partial outage affecting hosted text generation endpoints; not all models or requests are affected.
Current status: Mitigation in progress — errors decreasing after routing change.
Next update: in 15 minutes or on status changes.
```

ben (oncall): That reads well. Add note: No credentials/exposure, no change to customer data.

elaine (commops): Updated. Draft customer notification email/snippet:

"We are currently investigating increased error rates for text generation in our us-east-1 region. Our engineering team is actively mitigating the issue by routing traffic to a fallback model. Some requests may fail or have higher latency. We will provide an update within 15 minutes and notify you when full service is restored. If you rely on dedicated or reserved capacity, please contact support and we will escalate."

jordan (support): Can we give guidance for customers on temporary mitigations? e.g., switch to eu-west-1 or use dedicated capacity?

elaine (commops): Adding guidance: "As a temporary workaround, consider routing requests to another region (eu-west-1) or using a quantized model variant. See docs: https://redwood.dev/docs/region-routing"

fred (marketing): I’ll prepare social copy but want to wait until we have a clear status page update. Proposing short tweet for transparency:

"We're investigating increased error rates for text generation in us-east-1. Engineers are mitigating and we’ll share updates. Customers can route to other regions as a workaround. — Redwood Inference"

legal-bot: Reminder: any public messaging mentioning customer impact must be reviewed by Legal for compliance with SLAs if we call it an outage. Please ping legal@example.com for approval if you plan to tweet.

fred (marketing): Thanks. Looping Legal. Draft for blog/longer post (internal, hold):

"Timeline: 02:14 UTC — alert fired; 02:18 UTC — mitigation routing started; 02:22 UTC — errors reduced to mid-single digits; ongoing monitoring. Root cause under investigation (likely model-node memory pressure)."

alice (SRE): Can someone capture the min reproducible steps to add to postmortem? Right now: heavy concurrent KV-cache priming + large seq length requests hitting same model node — need to confirm.

dan (prodeng): We’ll snapshot kernels & memory dumps from node-17 and model-proxy logs. Assigning to dan and alice for RCA.

ben (oncall): Status update for status page (15m): errors decreased from 18% -> 4% after full routing to fallback. Rolling back full traffic to default model cautiously while monitoring.

carla (ops): Autoscaler ramped a warm pool by +6 nodes to absorb load, no errors on new nodes.

elaine (commops): Preparing final status page update for public: short, factual, and consistent with customer notice + tweet. Will post after legal ack.

fred (marketing): Proposed tweet (two-line):

"We experienced elevated error rates for text generation in us-east-1 earlier today. Engineers mitigated the issue by rerouting traffic; services are recovering. Read more on our status page: https://status.redwood.ai/INC-20260315-1042"

legal-bot: Legal review requested. Quick checklist: (1) confirm no SLA credit language; (2) ensure no admission of persistent downtime beyond facts. Assigned to legal-team — ETA 20m.

jordan (support): I’ll update the internal support playbook with the workaround steps and canned responses for customers. Please drop the final status copy here when posted.

ben (oncall): Follow-up: After 30m, error rate stabilized at ~1.2% and latency back to baseline. I’m going to hand off to next on-call (alice) for watch. Handoff notes: mitigation in place, RCA in progress (dan+alice), status page updated draft ready for final post.

alice (SRE): Taking over monitoring. If anything spikes I’ll escalate to infra and ops.

elaine (commops): Legal ack received: neutral language only, no SLA statement. Posting status page now and scheduling the short tweet. Final status page text:

"Incident INC-20260315-1042 — Resolved (2026-03-15T02:46 UTC)
Summary: Engineering routed traffic to a fallback model to mitigate elevated error rates in us-east-1. Error rates returned to normal and services recovered. Root cause: under investigation (memory pressure on a model serving node). No customer data exposure.
Impact: Partial outage for hosted text generation in us-east-1 affecting some requests.
Current status: Resolved; monitoring for recurrence.
Postmortem: A follow-up RCA will be published in the incident tracker."

fred (marketing): Tweet queued and approved. Will post once status page is live.

jordan (support): Internal playbook updated and support triage notified.

ben (oncall): Closing live incident duty. Leaving notes for postmortem and tagging logs: `INC-20260315-1042`

carla (ops): Removing canary routing, returning traffic to default routing slowly. All systems green in us-east-1.

alice (SRE): Thanks team. Postmortem owners: dan + alice. Communications: elaine + fred. Support followup: jordan. We’ll sync in async doc for RCA and publish within 72h. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident INC-20260315-1042 status changed to RESOLVED by ben. Duration: 32m.

elaine (commops): Posted status page and tweeted. Slack thread to close in 1h after postmortem stub created.

ben (oncall): Confirmed tweet live and support notifications sent. Good job everyone. :tada:"
